journeys.title: Publish an outage and watch it land
journeys.summary: Sam publishes an outage from the screen; a second screen sees it live; Sam resolves it and it leaves everywhere.

steps.text: First visit: no tenant is pre-filled. The header asks for the tenant your consumers read.
A second screen (Team B) already watches tenant journeys: the feed is empty and the badge says Live.
Pressing Publish with an empty form: the first invalid field gets focus and an error summary lists what is missing. Nothing was sent.
Sam fills in the outage: tenant, title, details, affected services, publisher.

journeys.summary: A maintenance window is published ahead of time, shows as Scheduled with a countdown, is turned active by the clock and closed at its end; another one is withdrawn before it starts.

journeys.title: A team attaches the sidecar to its app
journeys.summary: What the team adds to its manifests, and what it reads when the service does not show up.

steps.text: The Kustomize example rendered: the component adds the container and nothing else changes in the Deployment.
steps.transcript:
apiVersion: v1
data:
  CS_CLUSTER: ocp-east
  CS_ENDPOINT: https://communication.apps.example.com
  CS_TENANT: retail
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cs-health-sidecar
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: payments-api
  name: payments-api
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: payments-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: payments-api
        app.kubernetes.io/version: 1.4.2
    spec:
      containers:
      - image: registry.example.com/retail/payments-api:1.4.2
        name: payments-api
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /actuator/health/readiness
            port: 8080
      - env:
        - name: POD_NAME
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: metadata.name
        - name: POD_NAMESPACE
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: metadata.namespace
        - name: NODE_NAME
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: spec.nodeName
        - name: CS_SERVICE
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: metadata.labels['app.kubernetes.io/name']
        - name: CS_VERSION
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: metadata.labels['app.kubernetes.io/version']
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: cs-health-sidecar
        image: registry.example.com/platform/health-sidecar:1.0.0
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: cs-status
          periodSeconds: 30
        name: health-sidecar
        ports:
        - containerPort: 9465
          name: cs-status
          protocol: TCP
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: 50m
            memory: 32Mi
          requests:
            cpu: 10m
            memory: 16Mi
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          capabilities:
            drop:
            - ALL
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          runAsNonRoot: true
          seccompProfile:
            type: RuntimeDefault

journeys.title: The record book is unreachable
journeys.summary: The database goes away twice. Stopped (connections refused): the API answers 503 "database unavailable" within seconds, a feed opened meanwhile says Service degraded, readiness turns 503 while liveness stays 200, and everything resumes by itself. Frozen (connections hang): the open gap GAP-backend4-1, shown as it happens.

steps.text: The database container is stopped (jr-mongo): connections are refused.
A request while the database refuses connections: 503 after 5022 ms, with a plain message.
Readiness says not ready in 811 ms (take the pod out of traffic); liveness says alive (do not restart it).
Publishing now: the banner says the service cannot reach its database and recovers on its own; it took focus.
A feed opened during the outage: the badge says Service degraded (not Live) and the load error is announced as an alert.
The log: one WARN line per failed request, per skipped sweep and for the readiness change; no stack traces.

steps.text: The database is back: ready again, nothing restarted.
After Try again the list loads and the badge goes back to Live.
Now the database is frozen instead (docker pause): connections open but nothing answers.

Six requests while the database hangs: 503 after 20030 ms, 503 after 20031 ms, 503 after 20022 ms, 503 after 5014 ms, 503 after 5013 ms, 503 after 5010 ms. A 500 here is the open gap GAP-backend4-1: the driver pauses its connection pool and the error handler does not recognise that error, so the answer carries the driver's message, database address included.
